requirements.requirement: node2 and node3 each serve HTTP on TCP 8080 and identify which host answered
requirements.summary: A systemd 'simple-http' service running python3 http.server was installed and enabled on node2 and node3, serving index.html content identifying the node by hostname and IP. curl localhost:8080 on each returned 'Hello from node2 (10.100.122.11)' and 'Hello from node3 (10.100.122.12)' respectively. Post-restart checks confirm the services persist and answer correctly after reboot, and the after-executor lifecycle snapshot shows both nodes listening on 0.0.0.0:8080.

requirements.requirement: node1 presents one entry point on TCP port 80 of its management address that spreads requests across node2 and node3
requirements.summary: HAProxy was installed on node1 (OPNsense) via the os-haproxy plugin; config.xml was edited to add a frontend bound to 10.100.122.10:80 with a roundrobin backend pool containing node2 and node3 servers on port 8080. The generated haproxy.conf was verified (frontend bind 10.100.122.10:80, backend balance roundrobin with both servers), passed 'haproxy -c' syntax check, and the service was started and confirmed listening via sockstat on 10.100.122.10:80.

requirements.requirement: node4 receives answers from each of node2 and node3 through node1's single entry point
requirements.summary: From node4, 8 sequential curls to http://10.100.122.10:80/ produced a perfect alternating pattern of 'Hello from node2' and 'Hello from node3' responses, directly demonstrating load-balanced access via the single entry point. This was repeated identically after all four nodes were restarted, confirming the behavior persists post-reboot.

requirements.requirement: The new port-80 listener must be reachable without breaking existing management access (implicit outcome, since node4 successfully reaches it)
requirements.summary: pfctl -s rules confirmed a pre-existing pass rule for tcp/http (port 80) to self on vtnet0 alongside the untouched ssh pass rule, so no firewall change was needed; node4's successful curls to port 80 directly confirm reachability, and SSH access was clearly preserved since all subsequent executor commands over SSH succeeded.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide restart evidence protocol: node1 pre-restart healthy baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered service/data/cluster state
requirements.summary: Baseline kern.boottime (1788630765, 17:52:45) was captured, 'shutdown -r' was issued and acknowledged, SSH became unreachable during the transition (two timed-out attempts), then post-restart kern.boottime (1788631007, 17:56:47) proved a genuine reboot. HAProxy was confirmed running again and listening on 10.100.122.10:80, and node4 immediately reproduced load-balanced access through it.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide restart evidence protocol: node2 pre-restart healthy baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered service state
requirements.summary: Baseline boot_id (17b362d1...) was captured, reboot issued, post-restart boot_id (a81d7065...) differs confirming reboot, and simple-http service was confirmed active with curl localhost:8080 returning correct content afterward.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide restart evidence protocol: node3 pre-restart healthy baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered service state
requirements.summary: Baseline boot_id (29011044...) was captured, reboot issued, post-restart boot_id (dfe88611...) differs confirming reboot, with simple-http active and curl localhost:8080 returning correct content in the same post-restart command.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide restart evidence protocol: node4 pre-restart healthy baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered end-to-end access
requirements.summary: Baseline boot_id (b19a635d...) was captured, reboot issued, post-restart boot_id (20ccb9b0...) differs confirming reboot, and node4 successfully re-ran 8 load-balanced curls through node1 alternating between node2/node3, proving full end-to-end recovery.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are directly satisfied with strong, coherent evidence: node2 and node3 serve identifying HTTP content on 8080, node1 runs HAProxy presenting a single roundrobin entry point on 10.100.122.10:80, and node4 was shown alternating between both backends through that entry point both before and after a full sequential restart of all four nodes. The provider-wide restart evidence protocol is also fully satisfied for every node, with genuine pre/post boot-identity divergence, restart acknowledgements (including an observed SSH-down window on node1), and directly observed recovered service and end-to-end behavior, corroborated by the fixed before/after lifecycle snapshots. No unnecessary or unsafe executor mutations were identified.
limitations: The after_prepare snapshot is an alias of before_prepare (prepare was disabled for this task), so preparer-vs-executor state separation relies entirely on the executor timeline and the after_executor snapshot rather than an independent after_prepare capture.
Load-balancing distribution was only sampled via 8 sequential curls per check; while the pattern is a clean strict alternation consistent with roundrobin, a much larger sample was not captured.

operational_hygiene.summary: Reviewing all executor commands chronologically, mutating actions were: installing/enabling simple-http on node2/node3 (required backend), installing os-haproxy and editing config.xml with an automatic backup (.bak.haproxy) on node1 (required entry point), reloading/starting haproxy (required), and the four sequential node reboots (required by the fixed provider-wide restart protocol, not the public task, but bounded and expected). One inspection script (cmd-e1bdaff3bef34684) failed with a Python TypeError while read-only-probing the HAProxy.xml model; it made no writes and was immediately corrected by a follow-up read-only probe (cmd-fdb01863a16c47a5), so it is not a state-changing mutation. No unnecessary, destructive, retained, or security-weakening mutations were found; the config.xml backup file and /tmp/haproxy plugin directories are expected artifacts of the officially supported install/deploy path rather than executor residue. Firewall was left unmodified (an existing pass rule already permitted port 80), which is the minimal-footprint choice.
